observation_summary: The @InjectMocks annotation was failing to use property setters for dependency injection, defaulting to direct field access even when a setter was available.
hypothesis: The injection logic in FinalMockCandidateFilter was missing a step to attempt property setter injection before falling back to direct field injection.
prediction: The code would be updated to include a call to BeanPropertySetter before the existing FieldSetter call, with a conditional check to ensure the setter is used if successful.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the introduction of a BeanPropertySetter check that wraps the existing FieldSetter logic, confirming that the procedural order of injection attempts was the root cause.
reasoning_summary: The bug was a failure to prioritize property setters over field access during dependency injection. This is a procedural logic error in the injection algorithm. The fix involved adding a conditional check (BeanPropertySetter) to the existing injection procedure, which is a classic Algorithm/Method correction.
evidence_used: The fix diff shows the addition of 'if (!new BeanPropertySetter(fieldInstance, field).set(matchingMock))' before the existing 'new FieldSetter(fieldInstance, field).set(matchingMock);' call.
The bug report explicitly states: '@InjectMocks should carry out their work by the method (and not by field) if available'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a conditional check, the primary issue is the overall injection strategy (the algorithm) which was missing a step, rather than just a validation check on existing data.
This is a local procedural correction within the existing injection mechanism, not a design-level capability gap.
